note: Patch APPLY ORDER, declared. Both forks leave it implicit today — the Android fork encodes it in a
filename glob (`patches/mpv/*`), the darwin fork in the order of `patch -p1` lines inside a .nix string —
and ales-drnz encodes it in the body of a shell function with the constraint written only as a comment
("MUST run before strip_libass"). None of the three can be diffed against the others, which is how the
two forks came to apply the same patches in different orders without anyone noticing.
The `NNN-` prefix on a patch directory is stable IDENTITY, not order. It cannot be order: the darwin fork
applies its export-list patch BEFORE the libass strip, and the Android fork has no export-list patch at
all, so no single numbering can encode both platforms' sequences. Order is therefore declared here, per
dependency and per platform, and the workshop applies exactly this list in exactly this sequence.
Variants are not part of the key. Each patch declares which variants it belongs to in its own patch.json,
and the workshop filters this list by that: 002-remove-libass is audio-only, 009/010 are video-only, and
ORDERING CONSTRAINTS that are real and must survive an edit here:
* 002-remove-libass rewrites large regions of meson.build. 005-mpv-export-list also edits meson.build,
at library('mpv'). Darwin applies 005 first and that is the order reproduced here.
* 003-pcm-tap touches player/command.c in the audio-property region; 002-remove-libass touches the same
file at the libass-version property getter, ~2600 lines away. They are order-independent in practice,
and 003 runs last on both platforms anyway.
